decision_rule: rejected if the violation-difference interval lies at or below zero; supported if both intervals lie above zero; mixed if exactly one does; weakened otherwise
difference_definition: per seed, path-string group rate minus descriptor-anchored group rate, each group pooling its two adapters' counts within the seed
hypothesis: On held-out seeds, the descriptor-anchored adapters (dirfd-relative, strict-safe-open) have a lower completed containment-violation rate than the path-string adapters (lexical-prefix, canonicalize-then-open), and pay for it with lower availability under safe conditions.
null_hypothesis: The two adapter groups do not differ in completed containment-violation rate: the 95% interval of the per-seed difference includes zero.

predictions.statement: strict-safe-open records zero containment violations in the held-out run
dirfd-relative records zero containment violations on runs that did not take the fallback path
canonicalize-then-open records zero containment violations on primary-path runs in which no mutation fired

predictions.evidence: 48 of 48 adapter x family cells agree
predictions.statement: for every adapter and family, containment violations occur in the held-out depth region if and only if they occur in the in-distribution region

strict_safe_open_zero_violation_bound.caveat: treats runs as independent draws from the declared scenario distribution; they are deterministic functions of seeded parameters, so this is indicative only
